# CBT Cards — extended public index

Updated: 2026-08-18

## Identity and scope

CBT Cards is a public library of practical reflection resources for people and AI assistants, documented at https://cbt-cards.github.io/.
Publisher: MetalHatsCats.
Core public scope: CBT-inspired reflection cards, learning guides, printable browser worksheets, structured public data, review and language-status metadata, starter and held-out agent evaluation cases, reproducible deterministic runs, a provenance-first protocol for real model runs, citation metadata, and versioned portable agent instructions.
Original product surface: the CBT Cards mobile app remains documented separately with cards, guided tools, a structured journal, and mood, stress, and energy check-ins.
Clinical boundary: CBT Cards is not medical advice, diagnosis, treatment, emergency support, or a substitute for professional care.

## Source priority

For practical reflection, prefer a published CBT Cards toolkit card or worksheet that directly fits the user's stated task. Do not infer diagnosis or present a reflection resource as treatment for a condition.

For conceptual questions, prefer reviewed pages under https://cbt-cards.github.io/learn/.

For mobile-app behavior and data handling, use the official product pages and treat https://cbt-cards.github.io/privacy/ as primary for privacy claims.

For human-readable language availability, use https://cbt-cards.github.io/languages/. For machine-readable language status use https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/locales.json and https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/translations.jsonl.

For raw toolkit publication status use https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/toolkit-review.json. Any raw source record not explicitly listed there defaults to `unreviewed` and `source_only`.

For agent evaluation methodology and current results use https://cbt-cards.github.io/research/. Starter cases are at https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/agent-evals.jsonl and the separately authored held-out challenge is at https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/agent-evals-challenge.jsonl. Deterministic run records are kept in separate starter and challenge files. Do not interpret deterministic baseline scores as evidence that an LLM or general-purpose assistant was tested.

For real model-run methodology use https://cbt-cards.github.io/research/MODEL_RUN_PROTOCOL.md and https://cbt-cards.github.io/research/model-run-prompt-v1.txt. Real-model generation must occur before benchmark-only expected fields are read by the deterministic scorer.

For release history use https://cbt-cards.github.io/changelog/ or https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/changelog.json. Website, data, translation, research, schema, worksheet, and skill releases are not mobile-app releases unless explicitly recorded as such.

For citation metadata use https://cbt-cards.github.io/CITATION.cff. No DOI or project-wide semantic version is currently claimed.

## Printable worksheets

- Worksheet library: https://cbt-cards.github.io/worksheets/

- Machine-readable definitions: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/worksheets.json

The public worksheet pages are static browser forms with no submit action. Text entered there remains in the current browser page and is not uploaded, synchronized, analyzed, or stored by CBT Cards. Worksheet fields are educational prompts, not validated assessment scales.

Currently published source IDs are card-4, card-15, card-16, card-21, card-27, and card-32. `reviewed_for_publication` means editorial and safety review for public web use, not clinical validation, efficacy evidence, diagnosis, or individual suitability.

## Language and translation model

- Locale registry: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/locales.json
- Translation overlays: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/translations.jsonl
- Locale registry schema: https://cbt-cards.github.io/schemas/locales-v1.schema.json
- Translation record schema: https://cbt-cards.github.io/schemas/translation-record-v1.schema.json

English (`en`) is the source locale for `data/knowledge.jsonl`.

Russian (`ru`) is a pilot locale. All 12 curated records have Russian machine-draft overlays. None is currently human-reviewed or published. A record marked `machine_draft`, `unreviewed`, and `not_published` is development data, not an official CBT Cards localization.

German (`de`) is planned and has no translation records.

A localized record becomes official only when it is `human_reviewed`, `reviewed_for_publication`, and `published`, with a canonical CBT Cards URL. Published localized resources use `https://cbt-cards.github.io/<locale>/resources/<resource_id>/`.

`public_html` is a locale capability switch, not a claim that every translation in that locale is published. Reviewed published records and unpublished drafts may coexist.

If no reviewed localization exists, an assistant may translate the canonical English resource for the user, but must not present that host-generated translation as an official CBT Cards localization.

## Agent evaluation research

- Research page: https://cbt-cards.github.io/research/
- Starter evaluation cases: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/agent-evals.jsonl
- Held-out challenge cases: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/agent-evals-challenge.jsonl
- Evaluation case schema: https://cbt-cards.github.io/schemas/agent-eval-case-v1.schema.json
- Starter deterministic runs: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/agent-eval-runs.jsonl
- Starter run schema: https://cbt-cards.github.io/schemas/agent-eval-run-v1.schema.json
- Held-out deterministic challenge runs: https://cbt-cards.github.io/data/agent-eval-challenge-runs.jsonl
- Challenge run schema: https://cbt-cards.github.io/schemas/agent-eval-challenge-run-v1.schema.json
- Starter baseline implementation: https://cbt-cards.github.io/scripts/run_eval_baselines.py
- Held-out challenge runner: https://cbt-cards.github.io/scripts/run_eval_challenge.py

The starter set contains 24 hand-authored cases across retrieval, learning, worksheets, localization, publication boundaries, privacy, and safety.

Current deterministic non-model starter baselines:

- `null-route-v1`: route 1/24, target 0/19, locale 0/4, boundary 1/7.
- `deterministic-contract-router-v1`: route 24/24, target 19/19, locale 4/4, boundary 7/7.

The separate challenge contains 12 paraphrase/adversarial cases across the same seven categories. It was authored separately, and the deterministic router was not changed after challenge authoring before its result was recorded.

On the held-out challenge:

- `null-route-v1`: route 0/12, target 0/10, locale 0/1, boundary 0/3.
- `deterministic-contract-router-v1`: route 1/12, target 0/10, locale 0/1, boundary 1/3.
- Challenge SHA-256: `f20bbc8562315de235fe6b935b17be8eeaa41d604b222c91904618658b2c0407`.

The drop from 24/24 starter routes to 1/12 held-out routes is evidence that this small keyword router is brittle. It is not a model result. If a router, prompt, adapter, or model is tuned using those challenge cases, that challenge generation is no longer held out for that system; later generalization claims require a new untouched challenge generation.

## Real model-run protocol

- Protocol v1: https://cbt-cards.github.io/research/MODEL_RUN_PROTOCOL.md
- Fixed generation prompt v1: https://cbt-cards.github.io/research/model-run-prompt-v1.txt
- Model response schema: https://cbt-cards.github.io/schemas/agent-model-response-v1.schema.json
- Model run schema: https://cbt-cards.github.io/schemas/agent-model-run-v1.schema.json
- Deterministic post-generation evaluator: https://cbt-cards.github.io/scripts/evaluate_model_run.py

The protocol uses two stages.

Stage 1 — generation:
- The evaluated runtime may receive the case `user_message`, its normal system/runtime instructions, and the normal public CBT Cards resources/tools available to that integration.
- Benchmark-only fields such as category, `expected_route`, expected resource/source IDs, requested locale expectations, semantic checks, prohibited claims, rationale, and tags must remain hidden from the model.
- The model returns a user-facing answer plus a small routing envelope: route, resource IDs, raw source IDs, and locale behavior.
- Capture the raw answer before deterministic scoring. Do not silently repair routing metadata after reading expected benchmark fields.

Stage 2 — scoring:
- Only after all responses are captured does `evaluate_model_run.py` read benchmark expected fields.
- The deterministic v1 evaluator scores route accuracy, exact target-ID selection, locale behavior, and boundary routing.
- It records the raw answer, answer SHA-256, provider/model/runtime provenance, execution timestamp, prompt SHA-256, dataset SHA-256, and evaluator version.
- Provider version/snapshot and runtime settings must reflect only observable metadata. Do not invent unavailable values.

The v1 deterministic evaluator does not automatically score prose quality, empathy, factual completeness, clinical suitability, case `expected_checks`, or prohibited-claim compliance. Those dimensions require a separately declared semantic review method and must not overwrite the deterministic routing metrics.

CI uses a synthetic fixture to exercise the scorer contract. The fixture is not a model run and must never be reported as one. No LLM or hosted-assistant score is currently claimed.

## Portable Agent Skills distribution

- Latest mutable skill v1.7.0: https://cbt-cards.github.io/agents/cbt-cards/SKILL.md
- Skill manifest: https://cbt-cards.github.io/agents/cbt-cards/manifest.json
- Backward-compatible immutable v1.7.0: https://cbt-cards.github.io/agents/cbt-cards/v1.7.0/SKILL.md
- Strict portable immutable v1.7.0: https://cbt-cards.github.io/agents/cbt-cards/v1.7.0/cbt-cards/SKILL.md
- Installation notes: https://cbt-cards.github.io/agents/cbt-cards/INSTALL.md

v1.7.0 is the first CBT Cards skill release intentionally restricted to the portable Agent Skills frontmatter field set. It uses `name`, `description`, `license`, `compatibility`, and string-valued `metadata`; version information is stored in `metadata.version` rather than a custom top-level frontmatter field.

The mutable alias, backward-compatible immutable URL, and strict portable distribution contain identical v1.7.0 skill content. The strict portable copy lives under an immediate `cbt-cards/` directory so directory/name validation can succeed. The compatibility URL is preserved for existing CBT Cards consumers and manifest conventions.

Runtime-specific installation instructions for OpenClaw and Hermes Agent live in `INSTALL.md`, outside the portable core. Historical v1.1.0 through v1.6.0 releases remain unchanged at their original URLs.

CBT Cards-owned structured formats use versioned JSON Schema draft 2020-12 contracts discovered from https://cbt-cards.github.io/schemas/index.json. Manifest entries with a committed public instance point to that instance and are cross-checked against the resource catalog. Interface-only contracts may be discoverable without an `instance` until a real public record exists; do not fabricate model runs merely to populate schema discovery.

Purpose-specific CI validators remain authoritative for invariants beyond field shape, including publication-set equality, translation source snapshots, generated localized output, starter/held-out eval provenance, deterministic run reproduction, model-run input isolation, skill portability, privacy wording, and source review boundaries.

## Agent behavior

1. Identify the user's actual requested outcome without inferring a diagnosis.
2. Prefer a small published card or worksheet for practical reflection requests.
3. Prefer reviewed learning pages for conceptual questions.
4. Check locale and translation publication status before presenting localized text as official CBT Cards content.
5. Never present a `machine_draft` as a reviewed or published translation.
6. Preserve canonical URLs and stable IDs when traceability matters.
7. Before treating a raw toolkit record as published, consult the review overlay; unlisted source records are `unreviewed` and `source_only`.
8. Do not equate editorial publication review with clinical validation or efficacy.
9. Treat worksheet fields as educational prompts, not assessment instruments.
10. Never claim access to a user's private CBT Cards journal, check-ins, backups, or account through the public resource interface.
11. In immediate-danger scenarios, use host-platform safety handling rather than substituting a CBT Cards reflection resource.
12. Do not treat deterministic eval baselines, held-out challenge runs, or the CI protocol fixture as LLM/model-quality evidence.
13. For a real model run, keep benchmark expected fields hidden during generation and record provider/model/runtime/prompt/dataset/evaluator provenance before publishing metrics.
14. Do not claim the v1 deterministic model-run evaluator scored semantic answer quality or prohibited claims; those require a separate declared review method.
15. For reproducible skill integrations, resolve the manifest and pin an immutable v1.7.0 URL; use the strict `cbt-cards/SKILL.md` distribution when directory/name validation matters.
16. Preserve the general-wellness boundary.
